newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia to set debt rescheduling date in September.
newsitem.headline: Russia to set debt rescheduling date in September.

text.p: Russia plans to announce a closing agreement schedule with the London Club of commercial banks creditors by late September, but the level of reconciliations and bureaucratic wrangling could delay the process, a senior Finance Ministry official said on Friday.

"We are setting the goal by the annual meeting of the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank to tell the world about a concrete, tough closing schedule, but to do this we have to carry out a whole lot of procedures," Deputy Finance Minister Mikhail Kasyanov told Reuters.
The IMF and the World Bank annual meeting will take place in Hong Kong between September 21 and 24.

But Kasyanov said Russia still had problems in announcing the date as the volume of fully reconciled debt was still below 60 percent and the Finance Ministry had not yet passed documents on to the cabinet for approval.

"We cannot now announce the closing date as reconciliation is at the low level of less than 60 percent and the documents are not approved," he said."We want them to be approved, but it is not a fact that they will be approved."
Russia has to fully reconcile 90 percent of $24 billion principal of its total $35 billion debt to the London Club.
Kasyanov's pessimism contrasts with the positive reception given to news this week of the 60 percent figure, which sent MinFin bond prices to record levels.

MinFin dealers say the regular announcement of the figures starting this month brings transparency to the process and shows what progress Russia is making with reconciliation, which had not been clear until now.
